title: Пожар для отвлечения внимания  (A Fire to Create a Distraction)

segments.t: Sasha walks into the storage cooler and gasps when she finds Chef Barinov hiding inside, prompting him to swear her to secrecy. When Elena Pavlovna heads toward the cooler herself, Senya and Fedya set a pan ablaze and yell fire to distract her.
Луи, давайте, есть огнетушитель у вас?
Now let's break down each line of their conversation.
'You did not see me!' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'you' and finishing on 'saw'. Fedya answers right away.
'Who are you hiding from?' In Russian, the idea of 'and' flows naturally into 'whom' without extra filler words.
'Wait, what is going on over there?' Lyova brings out the contrast between 'and' and 'what' in a few short words.
'Fire, there is a fire!' Notice how Russian expresses 'flame' and 'fire' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Fedya answers right away.
'Why are you just standing there staring?' Fedya anchors the line on 'come on', while 'look' completes the thought.
'Do something!' In Russian, the idea of 'somehow' flows naturally into 'do' without extra filler words.
'Oh my goodness, you know what, we need to...' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'goodness' before landing on 'at'. Fedya answers right away.
Луи, давайте, есть огнетушитель у вас?
'Louis, come on, do you have a fire extinguisher?' Fedya chooses the respectful plural 'you' alongside 'you' to keep a polite distance.
'What kind of restaurant is this?' Lyova anchors the line on 'come on', while 'such' completes the thought.
'Into the walk-in fridge.' Senya brings out the contrast between 'refrigerator' and 'refrigerator' in a few short words. Fedya answers right away.
'I am going into the walk-in fridge.' The meaning hinges on 'go' working together with 'refrigerator' in spoken Russian.
'No need, just focus on the orders.' In Russian, the idea of 'not' flows naturally into 'orders' without extra filler words.
'You have to help me.' Notice how Russian expresses 'you' and 'to help' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Now let's put it all back together and hear the whole scene again.
Луи, давайте, есть огнетушитель у вас?
When you watch Scene 19 of Episode 14, listen out for the exchange around a fire to create a distraction — you will recognize every Russian phrase right away. See you in the next scene.
